title: Saints-49ers trade grades: New Orleans adds Zamir White after onslaught of RB injuries - CBS Sports
description: The Saints bolstered a running back group that saw Alvin Kamara and two others suffer preseason injuries
body:
The Saints bolstered a running back group that saw Alvin Kamara and two others suffer preseason injuries
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:21 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The second week of the NFL preseason closed with a trade. According to ESPN, the New Orleans Saints and San Francisco 49ers agreed to a deal that sends linebacker Deion Jones to the Bay Area in exchange for running back Zamir White. The transaction addresses depth for both teams, particularly for the Saints, with No. 2 running back Alvin Kamara nursing an MCL sprain.White signed with the 49ers less than two weeks ago. He inked a one-year deal worth $1.2 million and was projected to enter the season on the lower rungs of San Francisco's depth chart. Instead, he arrives in New Orleans with a chance to see playing time early in the campaign. White has never played a snap outside of Las Vegas, as he spent the first four years of his career with the Raiders and accumulated 736 rushing yards over 45 games.Jones landed on the Saints' roster a few days earlier on Aug. 7 by way of a one-year, $1.3 million contract. While he was an every-week starter for the Atlanta Falcons in each of his first six professional seasons, he filled a smaller role across three different teams over the last four years. Jones most recently played for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and tallied 29 tackles in 17 games last year.Below are trade grades for the Saints and 49ers.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Saints: B-Kamara's injury is a boon to Travis Etienne, who should take firm command of the No. 1 running back role in New Orleans if the former's absence carries into the regular season. It creates depth concerns in the backfield, though, especially since Kamara is not the only one on the shelf. Devin Neal aggravated a hamstring injury in Saturday's preseason game, and Audric Estime hurt his ankle in the preseason opener, leaving the Saints without the second, fourth and fifth options on their unofficial depth chart.
Adding White to the group should keep the running backs afloat through the end of training camp, and he is capable of eating up a few snaps in the opening weeks of the regular season if called upon.Boosting the running back depth without taking on any additional salary is a win for the Saints, especially since the linebacker they are parting with was no lock to make the roster in the first place. Jones was a cut candidate whom the team listed as a fourth-teamer.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    49ers: C+The 49ers were in need of linebacker depth with only Fred Warner and Tatum Bethune available to them, and Jones fits the mold of a third option. He could even push Bethune for the primary backup role, but the latter made eight starts in 2025 when Warner suffered his gruesome ankle injury and may still factor into the team's plans after making those important contributions.Regardless of how Jones fits into the equation, all San Francisco had to part with to acquire him was a deep backup who, at best, was sixth in line for carries. Removing players from behind Christian McCaffrey is always a risk given his extensive injury history, but the 49ers have plenty of more enticing backups they would turn to before White, who might not have even made the roster in the first place.
The team also just signed Khalil Herbert in a corresponding move to Patrick Taylor Jr.'s landing on injured reserve, so the cupboard is far from bare.

title: Raiders' Ashton Jeanty injured, helped off practice field, reportedly has sprained ankle - CBS Sports
description: The second-year running back was unable to put any weight on his right leg
body:
The second-year running back was unable to put any weight on his right leg
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:01 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        LAS VEGAS -- Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty was helped off the practice field on Sunday without putting any weight on his right leg.The second-year rusher had been having a strong practice when he landed awkwardly diving for a catch thrown by Kirk Cousins during 11-on-11 drills. His teammates immediately froze as he lay on the ground. Trainers tended to him, then helped him up and aided him off the field. As he left, the entire team got down on a knee and stayed silent for a while before finishing practice.The team did not immediately provide information on Jeanty's injury following practice.According to an ESPN report, Jeanty is believed to have sprained his ankle. The Raiders are still unsure how long he will be out, but it is not considered a long-term injury.Jeanty is coming off a quality rookie season in Las Vegas, totaling over 1,300 yards with 10 total scores.Throughout the day, Jeanty had been splitting reps with rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. It is presumed Washington will begin handling the first-team reps while Jeanty is sidelined.
The running back with the most rushing yardage on the Raiders roster as of now, besides Jeanty, is Dare Ogunbowale. 594 career rush yards, 850 career receiving yardsWashington capableIn his first NFL preseason action against the Arizona Cardinals, Washington Jr. ran six times for 63 yards, including a 53-yard run, and he proved that he can be utilized in pass protection and be a weapon in the passing game. He followed that up with another strong performance against the Houston Texans, running nine times for 56 yards and adding two catches for 18 yards. 
Should Jeanty have to miss any time due to injury, the Raiders seem to have a dependable back to take his place.

title: Ashton Jeanty uncertainty highlights Fantasy Football risers and fallers from Week 2 of the NFL preseason - CBS Sports
description: Most of the changes this week deal with injuries to Jeanty, Jayden Higgins and Alvin Kamara, but the Giants RB si
body:
Most of the changes this week deal with injuries to Jeanty, Jayden Higgins and Alvin Kamara, but the Giants RB situation requires monitoring.
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:54 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL's move towards more joint practices and less starter participation in the preseason has meant fewer big swings in my Fantasy Football projections. That's probably a good thing as it feels like more often the things we react to in preseason that aren't injury related end up being false signals or overreactions. So when talking about the big rankings movers of preseason Week 2, a lot of them came from events that happened before the games started on Thursday. Still, some of these moves are significant and may not be reflected in ADP for another week, so they are important to note if you have a draft coming up soon.Before we get to the definitive movers, I must at least mention that Ashton Jeanty left practice on Sunday and as of writing on Sunday we have no details regarding the severity of the injury. It's worth noting that our Dave Richard was at the practice and noted this: "His teammates immediately froze as he lay on the ground. Trainers tended to him, then helped him up and aided him off the field. As he left, the entire team got down on a knee and stayed silent for a while before finishing practice." It doesn't sound good, but again, we have no details. I would love to tell you to wait until we know more to react, but I know that (like me) many of you are drafting tonight. Jeanty was a borderline first round pick before the injury but until we know more I won't draft him before pick No. 35 in one-QB leagues. You can me more aggressive in more shallow leagues, or if you have a high tolerance for risk. At this moment there is both a chance he plays Week 1 and a chance he won't play all year. We just don't know. Those are terrible circumstances to draft under and you are going to have to make a decision based on your own risk tolerance.Jeanty's clear backup is Mike Washington Jr., and he has looked fantastic in the preseason. Washington has 119 rush yards on 15 carries in two preseason games and would be a Round 5 pick or higher if Jeanty's injury is indeed season ending. On Sunday night I am planning on looking for Washington in Round 8 assuming we don't have more information before I draft. Stay tuned, when we know more about this situation, you will. Here are the other movers from the past week:
Jayden Higgins injury falloutIt seems like more than a week ago, but the loss of Higgins is a big one for the Texans. He was having a spectacular offseason by all accounts. I boosted Nico Collins' target share slightly and he's now a Round 2 pick in full PPR leagues. The other wide receivers are very questionable with Tank Dell and Jaylin Noel battling injuries. Either is worth a pick in the final rounds of most drafts, but to start the season Xavier Hutchinson will probably be the team's second-best receiver. The biggest mover in my rankings was Dalton Schultz, who is now a borderline top-12 tight end worth a pick in Round 10. Schultz was second on the Texans with 106 targets last year, and that was on a team that threw 120 passes to Higgins and Christian Kirk, who is no longer on the team. If Dell or Noel don't step up then Schultz could flirt with 120 targets and a top-six finish at tight end. Najee Harris signing falloutIt has been a bad preseason for Tyrone Tracy and the acquisition of Harris only makes it worse. I am not entirely sure that Tracy has a role on this team, and for now I have dropped him outside of the first 10 rounds. Harris is worth a late-round pick, particularly in deeper leagues, but he has to get in football shape just to earn the secondary role to Cam Skattebo. Make sure Harris is rostered but don't draft him to be more than a backup. Skattebo becomes just a little riskier with this acquisition, because Harris is a coach's back and if the veteran regains form he could be a problem for Skattebo in both short yardage and the passing game. The safest course of action is to wait until Round 5 to draft Skattebo, but don't be surprised is someone in your league drafts him in Round 4.Alvin Kamara injury falloutIt has been a roller coaster offseason for Travis Etienne. He signed a big deal with the Saints and originally many of us thought that meant Kamara was leaving. When the team restructured Kamara's deal, Etienne fell into the mid-RB2 range. Now that Kamara may miss the start of the season I have Etienne ranked as a top-12 running back worth a pick in Round 3. While we do expect to see Kamara early in the year, he had already lost a step and I am very skeptical he'll be effective enough to stay on the field coming off this injury. I now have Etienne projected for 290 touches, and he has upside well beyond that.
Four smaller moves I made this past week:I remain the low guy on A.J. Brown, but I did move him up a few spots after his brilliant performance in team camp against Philadelphia. I am still worried about the knee and the volume, but I am no longer worried that he is not quite the same receiver he once was.Kyle Monangai fell behind Blake Corum and out of Round 8. His knee injury isn't supposed to last long into the season but I don't like that Week 1 is in question. D'Andre Swift remains one of my favorite picks in Round 4 and could move into Round 3 if we get a negative report on Monangai.Jalen Coker and Tetairoa McMillan look ready to dominate targets in Carolina and both look like they will get an elevated slot rate. I already had McMillan in Round 3, but I did move Coker up into Round 9 as a high-end WR4.Dalton Kincaid has maintained his health through the preseason and there is legitimate optimism that he plays the highest snap share of his career. That optimism pushes him into the top 12 tight ends for the first time this offseason. He would be a great guy to pair with Dalton Schultz in the double digit rounds. Schultz provides a nice floor and Kincaid has immense upside if he's ever a full time player.

title: Week 23 Fantasy Baseball Waiver Wire: Is Andrew Painter finally putting it all together? - CBS Sports
description: Progress isn't linear for any prospect, but that's especially true for pitchers. Injuries are just a fact of life when it comes to young
body:
Progress isn't linear for any prospect, but that's especially true for pitchers. Injuries are just a fact of life when it comes to young pitchers, and guys will occasionally go through stretches where they just completely lose the ability to throw strikes or lose their feel for certain pitches even when healthy.In Andrew Painter's case, it was a bit of an all-of-the-above situation. His career was derailed by an elbow injury just as it looked like he was about to make his MLB debut, and after two completely lost seasons, he came back from Tommy John surgery in 2025 and wasn't anywhere close to the same pitcher he was before the injury. Specifically, he went from having what was widely considered to be a plus fastball to having a pretty terrible one, and it led to a 5.26 ERA in Triple-A last season. And he wasn't any better this season. Despite breaking camp with the Phillies, Painter's fastball continued to be an issue and he was sent back down to Triple-A in mid-June with a 7.06 ERA. He went back down to the minors and continued to look pretty uninspiring, but a funny thing has happened in his past few starts since returning: He's starting to look like the pre-injury version of himself. You know, the one who was arguably the best pitching prospect in the game.We saw the absolute best version of Painter Saturday against the Cardinals, as he carved them up for eight strikeouts while allowing just one hit in seven innings. But it wasn't just the results that were worth getting excited about; it was how Painter actually pitched. Specifically, it was the fastball, which generated five swinging strikes on 15 swings, while sitting up at 97.3 mph on average and, most notably, generated two more inches of induced vertical break than his season average. 
That's no small thing; it takes Painter's fastball from a pretty mediocre shape to a very good one and helps explain why he suddenly started missing bats with the pitch. On the whole, Painter generated 20 swinging strikes in the start, led by his changeup, a new pitch Painter brought out in Triple-A after shelving his splitter.That changeup has looked solid since he came back, but it's the fastball that really stands out as a potential difference maker for Painter. For the most part this season, the only path to success for Painter seemed to be through limiting his fastball usage, as that pitch had a whiff rate around 10% and tended to get clobbered. It was a bad pitch, and if you have a bad fastball, it's hard to hide absent exceptional command of the rest of the arsenal. It's way too early to declare that Painter's four-seamer is suddenly a weapon. We're dealing with a sample size of just a couple of starts with better movement on the pitch, and a single start where he actually went out on the mound and dominated. That isn't nearly enough to change how we feel about any pitcher, especially one with as limited a track record of success at either Triple-A or the majors as Painter has.
But Painter's talent has never been in question, and if he's now figuring out how to maximize it, he could be very interesting. I'm not ready to say Painter needs to be active in your lineup every week the rest of the way, or even that he's a must-add pitcher in all leagues. But I do think if you're looking for someone with upside on the wire, he's about as good as they come right now, and he should probably be the top priority in any league when waivers run this week. Here's who else we're looking to add heading into Week 23. Week 23 Waiver TargetsCatcherTyler Stephenson, Reds (47%) Stephenson is hitting .253/.333/.527 with a 30-plus homer pace since the All-Star break, and with a .371 expected wOBA in that span, he has the underlying numbers to back it up. Stephenson has long been a fringe top-12 catcher, and even in the deeper state of the position in 2026, he's not a bad one, even if he's generally more "good enough" than a true difference-maker. But that's a nice floor for a guy who is this hot right now.Deep league option: Rafael Flores, Pirates (21%) – There's an awful lot of swing-and-miss in Flores' game right now, but you can overcome that by just mashing the ball, and that's certainly what he's doing right now. Since the start of August, he is hitting .268/.333/.659 and while his underlying numbers don't entirely back it up, his 91.4 mph average exit velocity in that span is a sign that the power is real, at least. He's a fine upside play for your No. 2 catcher spot right now.
First BaseAbimelec Ortiz, Nationals (41%)The biggest thing holding Ortiz back right now is the fact that the Nationals are treating him like a true platoon player, with just five of his 60 plate appearances coming against lefties. But he's absolutely crushing righties right now, with a .250/.291/.577 line and five homers in 55 trips to the plate. He makes enough contact, hits the ball hard, and elevates it well, all skills that are going to keep Ortiz relevant even if his upside is limited by the role right now. That makes him more of a corner infield option than a 1B in most Fantasy leagues, but that's still worth chasing. Deep league option: Ralphy Velazquez, Guardians (17%) – This is a stash, but I think one we're going to see at some point. The Guardians have done well to get something out of Nate Lowe, but Velazquez has the kind of skill set that can absolutely give them a much-needed boost down the stretch. It might take until roster expansion on Sept. 1, but Velazquez just had a three-homer game Saturday down at Triple-A and is hitting .381 with 14 homers in 16 games in August and just clearly doesn't have anything left to learn down there. For a team very much in desperation mode for a playoff spot, there should be room for him in the lineup.Second BaseAngel Genao, Guardians (35%) Genao has been a nice sparkplug for the Guardians, filling in wherever needed in the infield and hitting .315/.373/.426 through his first 15 MLB games. It hasn't been the most Fantasy-friendly skill set yet – just one steal and one homer – but he's also making a ton of contact and putting up a 92 mph average exit velocity, so there's a lot to like about the skill set without even factoring in the fact that he's eligible at third and shortstop as well as second base. At the very least, he's a great player to have around on your bench for the stretch run with that kind of flexibility, and he certainly won't hurt you as a starter. 
Deep league option: Pedro Ramirez, Cubs (13%) – Ramirez is slumping at a bad time, as it coincides with Dansby Swanson's injury pushing him into the full-time role we've been waiting for. Still, he's eligible at the two weakest positions in Fantasy and looks like he's going to play every day in one of the best lineups in baseball for the foreseeable future, so he's worth taking the flier on in deeper leagues.Third BaseAlec Bohm, Phillies (66%) Bohm has always been a pretty boring hitter even at his best, but he has also always had the skill set to be very useful for Fantasy when he's locked in thanks to the amount of contact he makes in the lineup he's in. He was awful for much of the season, but he is now hitting .336 since the All-Star game, leading to 28 RBI in his past 32 games. His underlying skill set has looked a lot more stable all along than his actual production would make you think, and while he likely won't keep hitting .340 forever, Bohm is definitely capable of running big batting averages and driving in a ton of runs for long stretches, making him a perfectly fine hot-hand play here.  Deep league option: Jordan Lawlar, Diamondbacks (35%) – I wasn't sure the Diamondbacks would play Lawlar every day once he came back from the IL, but he started each of the first four games back before a breather on Saturday (he was back in on Sunday), so it looks like they're going to keep running him out there in center field. Lawlar is still just 24 and has hit .283/.356/.434 with a 20-homer, 40-steal pace in his very small sample size of healthy games this season. I don't think he's actually that good, but I do still have hope that Lawlar can be a very good Fantasy option, especially in Roto leagues. 
ShortstopKaelen Culpepper, Twins (32%)There's been some swing-and-miss in Culpepper's game so far, which isn't terribly surprising. Despite the 28% strikeout rate, however, he has still managed to hit .286/.340/.452 in his first 12 MLB games with a couple of homers and a very strong 90.9 mph average exit velocity. We'll need to see him run a bit more to truly live up to his potential, but he's showing some upside in his first taste of the majors, at least.Deep-league option:  Trevor Story, Red Sox (37%) – Expectations shouldn't be terribly high for Story, who was having an awful season long before he underwent surgery to repair a hernia in mid-May. But he's on the verge of returning from his injury – it could be as soon as this week, in fact! – and let's not forget that he was a must-start Fantasy option in all formats in 2025, when he hit .263/.308/.433 with 25 homers and 31 steals. It's not even clear if Story is going to play every day when he returns for the Dodgers, but if he can tap into even a little bit of the upside he showed last season, he could provide a huge boost down the stretch. If you have the roster spot to play with this week, why not add him and see what happens? OutfieldWalker Jenkins, Twins (35%)Like with Velazquez, it seems like we're well past the point where the Twins should give him a chance. Injuries have threatened to derail Jenkins' career as a prospect, but he has nonetheless managed to get to Triple-A as a 21-year-old and hit .298/.396/.496 – before he homered twice Sunday, his third multi-homer game in the past three weeks. He is 27 for 65 with 10 extra-base hits in 16 August games, with 10 walks to 12 strikeouts, and he's even thrown in five steals for good measure. There clearly isn't much left for him to learn down there, and while the Twins don't necessarily have any obvious holes in the outfield, Trevor Larnach isn't so essential that they couldn't push him to the side to give a talented youngster a chance during a playoff race where they need to prioritize upside to make up lost ground. Jenkins has an advanced approach at the plate and could be a Fantasy difference-maker if this power breakout is for real. I suspect we'll see him in the next week or so. 
Zac Veen, Rockies (38%) The Rockies are mostly treating Veen as a platoon bat right now, which is disappointing but not entirely surprising given how crowded things have been for them in the outfield. He's not helping his case by striking out nearly 45% of the time so far, but he has managed to be productive in spite of that and remains a young talent worth betting on in deeper leagues. Cam Smith, Astros (45%) Smith is about to finish his second full season in the majors and he isn't yet 24, which is to say, he almost certainly isn't a finished product. It's been a disappointing and frustrating first two seasons, to be sure, but there have also been bright spots amid the frustration, especially lately. Smith is starting to elevate the ball a bit more consistently lately, bumping his flyball rate to 41% so far in August, leading to four homers in 18 games entering play Sunday, notably without an increase in his strikeout rate. Smith has long had all of the physical tools, but he hasn't optimized his swing to take advantage of that. What if he's starting to? Given the upside inherent to a guy with some of the best bat speed in the majors, why not add him and see if he's starting to figure it out? Especially when the underlying data has been better than his actual production all season? There's something here. Griffin Conine, Marlins (36%) The Marlins are giving Conine a longer leash lately and he isn't looking overwhelmed. I mean, sure, you could point to his 31% strikeout rate in the month of August and make the case, but that's a pretty typical mark for Conine, so we'll take it during one of the first stretches of his career where he's starting to face lefties a little more often (starting three of five against lefties in August). The Marlins are set to face four lefties this week, so don't be shocked if he sits at least once or twice, but I'd guess he also starts at least two of those games, and his power could make up for sitting out a couple. 
Luis Robert, Mets (64%)Robert has been pretty hit-or-miss since coming back from the IL, with his seven homers in 27 games standing in pretty stark contrast to his .266 OBP in that time. That all-or-nothing approach makes him a tough fit in points leagues, and the lack of stolen bases limits his utility in Roto, too. But the power has been impactful enough to bet on, even if he isn't the star he once was. Starting PitcherJacob Lopez, Athletics (40%)Fantasy players aren't rushing out to add Lopez, but they probably should be. Remember, he had a long stretch last season where he looked like a must-start pitcher before suffering an elbow injury, and he's looked a lot like that version of himself lately. He has at least eight strikeouts in three of his past five starts, with 37 strikeouts to just seven walks and a 2.76 ERA in that stretch. He pitches for a bad team in a tough home ballpark, but Lopez has shown the ability to both miss bats and limit hard contact despite a sky-high flyball rate, and I don't think his success is a fluke. There might be a relatively slim margin for error – he succeeds more on funk than pure velocity or stuff – but when he's locked in, Lopez gives hitters fits, and he's very locked in right now. George Klassen, Angels (20%)I know people are pretty excited about Klassen, but I'm gonna be honest: I don't really see it. I'm not saying he's bad, let alone useless, but I'm not sure I buy him as someone who is going to be worth trusting moving forward. He found more success in Triple-A than his 3.96 ERA would make you think – league average in the PCL is 5.50, mind you – and he does come to the table with a legit fastball/slider combo, so he has the stuff to succeed in the majors. But he's also never really thrown strikes at an acceptable rate, so the four walks in 13 innings over his last two starts are going to be tough to replicate. But the stuff is good enough to at least be worth a look to see if he can keep it going, especially with a two-start week coming up in Week 23. 
Grayson Rodriguez, Angels (26%)I don't have a ton of faith in either Angels pitcher, if we're being honest, but I think Rodriguez is about as interesting as Klassen. We've seen a couple of good starts from him lately, most recently Thursday's against the Astros, when he struck out six over seven innings while allowing just two unearned runs, and he's now down to a 3.27 ERA with 25 strikeouts to nine walks in 22 innings in four August starts, and his final start of July was pretty good, too. Rodriguez's fastball has played down for much of the season, but it's been a lot more effective when paired with his changeup lately, and while you'd like to see another pitch step up and prove more reliable for him, right now, it's been good enough. Tyler Mahle, Braves (68%) Sometimes, baseball is simple. Sometimes you go to a new team and they just tell you, "Hey, why don't you throw your best pitch a whole bunch more?" and then you do it, and then you start pitching a lot better. Mahle has thrown his splitter 38% of the time since getting to the Braves, up from 25% with the Giants, and he's seen a massive spike in his strikeout rate (to 28%) and arguably the best stretch of his season as a result. He isn't a true-talent sub-2.00 ERA pitcher, obviously – his 4.80 xERA should give ample reason for skepticism – but Mahle has had stretches like this before, including most of 2025, so why not just keep riding it until the wheels come off?Joe Musgrove, Padres (43%) Musgrove is close to returning, though after he was tagged for five runs in his most recent rehab start, it sounds like the Padres are going to send him out on one more start in the minors before he returns. He hasn't pitched in the majors in 23 months and has had a bumpy road back from Tommy John surgery, but his fastball velocity during his rehab stint has been up to 95 mph, higher than any season in his MLB career, so I'm very interested to see what Musgrove looks like when he finally makes his return. He could make a real impact down the stretch. 
Relief PitcherKodai Senga, Mets (39%)The Mets gave Senga a real test Sunday, asking him to pitch in back-to-back games for the first time … and he gave up a game-winning homer to Tristan Peters to cost the Mets the game. That's a bummer, and it's fair to wonder if his faltering in his first time trying to pitch on consecutive games might lose him some of the faith he has earned lately. On the other hand, Senga has still allowed just two runs in 7.1 innings since moving to a full-time bullpen role, while striking out nine amid a velocity spike, so I think he's earned a longer leash than this. We'll see how he responds to this, but I'd bet on Senga's next appearance coming in a save situation – albeit probably after a few days of rest. Nate Pearson, Royals (3%)The Royals have been searching for an answer in the ninth inning basically ever since Carlos Estevez's velocity was way down during the spring, and Pearson is the latest arm to get a try, with two of the team's past four saves, including one Friday this weekend. Steven Cruz was lined up to pitch the ninth in a save situation before the Royals scored twice in the ninth Sunday, so I don't think we can just declare that Pearson is the Royals closer now or anything. But he's in the mix and he might be as talented as anyone in the bullpen if he can stay healthy and throw strikes. Pearson is a bit of a long shot to make a difference, but if Cruz falters, Pearson definitely looks like he'll get a shot.

title: Scottie Scheffler reveals hand, foot and mouth disease struggles at BMW Championship - CBS Sports
description: The world No. 1 was nowhere near 100% this week in St. Louis during the second leg of the FedEx Cup Playoffs
body:
The world No. 1 was nowhere near 100% this week in St. Louis during the second leg of the FedEx Cup Playoffs
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:25 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Scottie Scheffler revealed late Sunday that he struggled during competition at the 2026 BMW Championship while dealing with the impact of hand, foot and mouth disease. Scheffler, who completed his tournament at 7 under, played with blisters in his throat and on his hands, making it difficult to grip his clubs.Still, the world No. 1 fought his way inside the top 15 in the penultimate event of the season and the second leg of the FedEx Cup Playoffs.Scheffler called himself stubborn, citing that characteristic and the importance of the BMW Championship as reasons he played all four rounds rather than withdrawing from the tournament to heal for next week's Tour Championship. He powered through and improved as the week progressed, registering three straight under-par rounds after an opening 72."I got the hand, foot, mouth," Scheffler said. "So, you get blisters on your hands and in your throat and on your feet. So, to start the week, it was pretty painful to grip the club. If I was smarter, maybe I would have pulled out, but I was playing so good, I felt like, if I could knock it out quickly and just get through the first couple rounds, I would still have a chance."But I think that's part of my stubbornness, probably. That's probably a strength of mine and a weakness at times. Like, I've never been one to ever pull out of a tournament, especially in the middle of it. That's really frustrating for me. So, I definitely didn't want to do that going into this week, even though it was suggested. But I'm proud of how I fought. 
"Feel like I'm starting to heal up. My throat is still bugging me pretty good, but my hands feel normal today. I actually almost caught myself shaking hands with Cam [Young] on 18; I would have felt really bad. I was like, 'Oh, my gosh, I almost forgot.' So that's good news, starting to feel better. Hopefully, the throat will clear up [over] the next couple days."Hand, foot and mouth disease is a virus that spreads easily from person to person through bodily fluids. It most commonly affects children under age 5, and adults often catch it from infected children, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The Schefflers have two children, each under 3 years old.Although he did not successfully defend his BMW Championship title, Scheffler did finish the week as No. 1 in the FedEx Cup standings, securing his place atop the bonus money distribution list. He will look for even more next week at the Tour Championship, where -- though every player will start at even par -- Scheffler's name will be among the short list of potential winners.
"Walking's fine," Scheffler confirmed. "Once you get on the course, you get the adrenaline and everything, I started to feel better. But the blisters on hands was probably the most challenging, just because it was painful to grip the club to start the week. I was prioritizing rest, so I wasn't able to work out the way I want to and practice the way I want to and even warm up for rounds the way I want to. I really just did my best to try and battle, and it maybe was a poor decision playing, but I've never been one to try and quit."

title: Mike Vrabel makes surprising admission about Patriots' roster - CBS Sports
description: Vrabel's team apparently has a pretty big deficiency entering the 2026 season
body:
Vrabel's team apparently has a pretty big deficiency entering the 2026 season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:57 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Following his team's preseason win over the Eagles, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel made an honest acknowledgment about his team that is typically something that wouldn't be heard from a coach, let alone one that is coming off a Super Bowl appearance. Vrabel's surprising assessment of his team came after he was asked about resting his starters for a second straight preseason game. Instead of breezing past the question with a non-answer, Vrabel went with the direct approach. "I don't think we have a very deep team, Mike," Vrabel said while addressing the reporter who asked the question. "So, you know, I think we have to make sure that we're preparing our football team, and that we're doing everything that we can to keep our best players available. And if that means playing Thursday (in New England's final preseason game) as part of preparation, that's what we'll do. Have not made that decision yet, but I would say that that's something that I'm confident in with where we're set up currently." Vrabel's admission quickly generated attention on social media, and for good reason. He essentially said that he is keeping his starters out of preseason games because the Patriots can ill afford to lose any of their starters, as they currently do not have the depth necessary to replace them. 
That's troubling on several levels, most especially because, in a physical sport like football, depth is a critical component to a team. It's one of the biggest things a team needs to have in order to endure the rigors of a 17-game regular season and a three- or four-game postseason. Options for improvementFortunately for Patriots fans, the team's apparent lack of depth can improve. New England will have the ability to sign a slew of players who will be available at the end of the preseason when teams make their initial 53-man roster cuts. The Patriots can also trade for players from other teams at any time until November 10. Another option, and the most tangible one, is for Vrabel and his staff to continue coaching up the backups who currently make up the roster. Part of that, Vrabel said, will involve working on consistency and not making the same mistake twice. 
"As far as some of the younger guys, we need to make new mistakes, because you need to be able to count on some of these guys when we put the roster together to be able to contribute," Vrabel said. "I think that there's a lot of ebbs and flows in a professional football game. How can you handle making a mistake? How can you handle getting blocked? How can you handle being a good play and then coming back and being able to do it again? "How they bounce back, how they handle different situations, what they do in live action, I think is really critical."From a depth perspective, one notable positive from Saturday's game was second-year running back Lan Larison. Larison, a former undrafted rookie who suffered a season-ending foot injury last preseason, had 12 touches for 74 yards that included a touchdown run and a 28-yard reception. 
"I felt like Lan certainly had a good performance," Vrabel said. "A gritty, tough, performance tonight. He did some really good things."

        Right-handed starting pitcher Casey Mize, one of the San Diego Padres' most crucial additions leading up to the recent trade deadline, was forced to exit his Saturday start after injuring his ankle on the dugout steps. Mize sprained his right ankle – his "drive" leg off the mound – while descending the dugout steps between the second and third innings of his start against the Twins, an eventual 7-5 win for San Diego. Mize went out for the third inning after having his ankle taped, but was unable to complete the frame. "I think my spike got caught on like the edge of the step, I guess, and then it kind of just made me slip a little bit," Mize said after the game, via MLB.com. "I tried to catch myself, and I ended up rolling my ankle kind of on the bottom step there."
Imaging on his injured ankle was negative, and Mize is classified as day-to-day for now. In that Saturday start, Mize allowed four runs total and three home runs in 2 ⅔ innings of work. He now has a 7.00 ERA after four starts with the Padres. However, his pre-trade work with the Tigers – a 2.70 ERA and 2.56 FIP over 16 starts – gives him a strong overall body of work this season. The 29-year-old Mize is slated for free agency this coming offseason, but first his focus will be on getting back on the mound and helping the Padres qualify for the playoffs for the fifth time in the last seven years. 
At present, the Padres under first-year manager Craig Stammen are 70-60 and in third wild-card position in the NL. They're also 14-6 thus far in August.

title: Grading every rookie QB from NFL preseason Week 2: Fernando Mendoza lackluster - CBS Sports
description: Of the 15 rookie quarterbacks who saw action this week, a small handful put on a show
body:
Of the 15 rookie quarterbacks who saw action this week, a small handful put on a show
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:50 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        There are only a couple of quarterbacks in the 2026 rookie class who can realistically expect to play in NFL games this season. Of that group, only No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is virtually guaranteed to have the opportunity to start. Strong showings in the preseason can go a long way in increasing the number of first-year quarterbacks who carve out meaningful roles on their respective teams, though.For most of the professional newcomers who have been in action over the last two weeks, impressive preseason showings will help them latch onto rosters as second or third options. Take Joey Aguilar or Jalon Daniels, for instance. Both scored touchdowns in consecutive outings, and Daniels oversaw a comeback win for the Buccaneers in preseason Week 2. They could go from undrafted free agents to important depth pieces because of their strong play.There were 15 rookie quarterbacks in action during the second week of the preseason. Some started, others entered the lineup during the second half, and one saw less than a minute of action.
        
            
                NFL preseason Week 2 overreactions: Shedeur Sanders will start for Browns, Jets' defense is fixed
                
                    Carter Bahns                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Below are grades for each of those rookie quarterbacks who played in Week 2.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Fernando Mendoza, RaidersGrade: DAdjusting from college football to the NFL is hard. Do not let one rough preseason game against a stellar defense get in the way of Fernando Mendoza's potential to find ample success as a pro, potentially as soon as the latter stages of his rookie year. It really was a tough one, though. The No. 1 overall pick threw a pick-six that went 80 yards the other way on the Raiders' opening possession, and he finished his first start 8-for-15 for 86 yards. He also took a sack for a loss of 11 yards. Mendoza did not reduce the gap between him and Kirk Cousins, but that was never the goal of this preseason. Las Vegas has no reason to rush him into the lineup.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cade Klubnik, JetsGrade: BGeno Smith gave Cade Klubnik a tough act to follow when he completed all seven of his passes and scored a touchdown, but his potential backup held his own against a Steelers defense that forced all kinds of pressure on the pocket. Klubnik did not orchestrate any scoring drives but helped the Jets get into field goal range during a two-minute drill at the end of the first half. He spent most of his time on his own half of the field and took two sacks, but it was not as if he received much help from his offensive line. A 16-yard keeper went down as New York's longest rush of the day.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Drew Allar, SteelersGrade: CIt was always going to be a massive ask for Drew Allar to replicate the kind of magic he sparked in his professional debut. He did not come particularly close to repeating that three-touchdown effort. The most positive takeaway from Week 2 was that he went turnover-free; Will Howard, in comparison, threw two interceptions before giving way to his backup. Allar took three sacks and completed fewer than 50% of his 23 throws, and the Steelers gained just six first downs with him under center in the second half. If there was anything to build on, it was a 38-yard strike to rookie tight end Lake McRee.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Joey Aguilar, JaguarsGrade: AThere is some arm talent in Joey Aguilar. A week after he delivered a 43-yard dart on the lone throw of his professional debut, he connected with Trebor Pena on a 29-yard touchdown. Aguilar's highlights have come in the second half against reserve defenses, but they are meaningful nonetheless for an undrafted free agent fighting for a roster spot. In total, he threw just one incompletion across 10 attempts against the Panthers and racked up 130 yards plus the scoring play.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Athan Kaliakmanis, CommandersGrade: BFor the second consecutive week, Athan Kaliakmanis went down as the Commanders' passing leader. It was an even wider margin this time around as he outdid Sam Hartman, 162 yards to 67, despite throwing just three more passes than his fellow backup. The first play of the fourth quarter was the source of one-third of those yards as he delivered a 55-yard strike down the sideline to Nick Nash. Outplaying Hartman in two chances, albeit without a touchdown drive, gives Kaliakmanis a chance to lock down Washington's No. 3 role.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Luke Altmyer, LionsGrade: CProgress. Luke Altmyer was clean in the turnover department in the 17-13 win over the Commanders, which is a step in the right direction after he tossed a pair of interceptions in his debut. Taking four sacks, however, gives the Illinois product something new to work on. Chalk some of that up to the offensive line, since he was under pressure for most of his outing. Altmyer did not take a step toward the No. 2 job but should latch on as a third option with the potential to develop into more.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jack Strand, FalconsGrade: AThe Falcons might just have something in Jack Strand. He arrived in Atlanta as a relative unknown, having gone undrafted out of Division II Minnesota State–Moorhead, but he made a name for himself in two preseason outings. Following the rushing touchdown he logged in Week 1, Strand erupted for 212 passing yards, a touchdown and another score on the ground in a drubbing of the Colts. He and Cooper Rush combined to complete 16 of their first 17 throws, and his rushing ability (22 yards on nine carries) is obvious and differentiates him in the battle for the No. 3 quarterback job.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Joe Fagnano, RavensGrade: AJoe Fagnano is racking up the volume this preseason. The Ravens clearly want to find out what they have in the undrafted signal-caller, considering they gave him 48 passing attempts across two games. On one of those throws in Week 2, he accounted for the lone touchdown of the 13-3 win over the Vikings with an 8-yard scoring toss to LaJohntay Wester. Fagnano converted on 75% of his passes (which, amazingly, was a regression from Week 1) and showed off a little bit of mobility, too. Everything points to Fagnano taking the No. 3 role from Austin Reed.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Ty Simpson, RamsGrade: BTy Simpson swapped roles with Stetson Bennett IV this week after handling the lion's share of work in Week 1. The reduced workload limited him in his attempt to recreate the 21-for-25, two-touchdown clinic he put on the week prior, but he still found a rhythm and oversaw two lengthy drives in his three possessions of action. Both went 11 plays, and while the first ended in a turnover on downs, the Rams capped off their final series with a touchdown in the 34-0 blanking of the Saints.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Mark Gronowski, DolphinsGrade: DMark Gronowski's greatest asset is his ability to make plays on the ground, and he got two chances to show it in his pro debut. He took two carries for nine yards, which is the only thing he had to write home about after gaining just one yard through the air on five attempts. Each of his three possessions were three-and-outs. The extremely limited playing time Gronowski has seen this preseason does not bode well for his chances of making the roster, not to mention his ineffectiveness on Saturday.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Miller Moss, BearsGrade: CFormer college teammates reunited in Chicago when Miller Moss signed with the Bears as an undrafted free agent, and both he and his former USC pal Caleb Williams saw the field in Week 2. Moss' role increased from the week prior, when he threw just eight passes, as he tossed a team-high 21 of them in the loss to the Bengals. His final line was solid, but they were mostly empty numbers as four of his drives ended in punts, one resulted in a missed field goal, and another concluded with a turnover on downs.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cole Payton, EaglesGrade: IncompleteCole Payton was a darling of Week 1 with his passing touchdown and 45 rushing yards, but he hardly had an opportunity to show off those dual-threat skills again this weekend. Payton came in for the Eagles with 57 seconds to play, had a completion scrapped for a penalty, connected on a 10-yard pickup and finished off his short day with a strip sack.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Behren Morton, PatriotsGrade: AAfter Tommy DeVito worked the first half, Behren Morton took all the second-half snaps in the Patriots' 24-21 win over the Eagles. That timeshare gave him the opportunity to flex his clutch gene. The second of his two touchdown drives decided the game. Trailing 21-17 with about a minute to play, Morton unleashed a 37-yard ball to Nick DeGennaro, who beat his defender to get into the end zone for the game-winner. It put the final touches on a splendid 13-for-17 day for Morton in which he accumulated 129 yards through the air.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Garrett Nussmeier, ChiefsGrade: BGarrett Nussmeier still awaits his first professional touchdown. The opportunities have been there across two games, but 36 passes between the two were not enough to provide that breakthrough. He went 9-for-17 for 74 yards and led a scoring drive, which ended in an Emmett Johnson touchdown run. That was in addition to a 13-play possession that produced a field goal. It was nothing spectacular individually, but Nussmeier kept the chains moving and put points on the board.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jalon Daniels, BuccaneersGrade: AIn Week 1, Jalon Daniels scored his first rushing touchdown. In Week 2, he found the end zone for the first time through the air. The Kansas product has been tough for defenses to bring down, as he remains sackless through two games and tacked on 19 rushing yards across seven carries in his latest outing. A 9-0 halftime deficit evaporated when the Buccaneers inserted Daniels in the second half, as he orchestrated three scoring drives and lifted Tampa Bay past the Chiefs by a point. It is hard to ask for a whole lot more than that.

Linebacker Trent Hendrick has committed to UCLA, according to Bruin247, giving the Bruins a veteran addition to the middle of their defense less than two weeks before the start of the 2026 season.Hendrick's return to college football comes after a Louisiana court granted him a temporary restraining order against the NCAA last week, allowing the veteran linebacker to receive an additional season of eligibility and enter the transfer portal outside the normal transfer window.

Hendrick, who participated in the Cleveland Browns' minicamp in May, exhausted his collegiate eligibility following the 2025 season but was among a group of players who challenged the NCAA's five-for-five eligibility rule. The court ruling opened the door for him to pursue another college opportunity, and he quickly became one of the most sought-after players available.He ultimately chose UCLA, reuniting with Chesney, who coached Hendrick at James Madison for two seasons before taking over the Bruins in December. Hendrick becomes the 11th player to follow Chesney from James Madison to UCLA.Trent Hendrick was a dominant force for James Madison.

                                                            Hendrick brings experience to Bruins defenseHendrick also becomes the most experienced player on UCLA's roster, having logged 1,808 career FBS snaps.

He was named the conference's Defensive Player of the Year in 2025 after helping lead the Dukes to the College Football Playoff.The 6-foot, 234-pound linebacker finished last season with 106 tackles, three sacks, three pass breakups and two forced fumbles.His combination of production and experience made Hendrick one of the most intriguing players among those seeking additional college eligibility. 247Sports' college football transfer portal analyst Cooper Petagna ranked Hendrick No. 2 on his list of players who received eligibility relief, noting that his "institutional knowledge could help curb the learning curve" at his next destination.

title: Browns' Todd Monken says Deshaun Watson's comments won't impact QB decision - CBS Sports
description: Watson called Browns fans 'disrespectful' following Saturday's loss
body:
Watson called Browns fans 'disrespectful' following Saturday's loss
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:14 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        While it appeared that Deshaun Watson's postgame comments all but ended his chance at winning his position battle over Shedeur Sanders, Browns coach Todd Monken said that they will not be factored into his decision. Monken added that he plans to announce who will be the team's starting quarterback on Monday. Watson followed up his poor performance during Saturday's loss to the Bills by taking aim at fans who booed him during the game. Saturday was Watson's first game in front of Cleveland's home fans since his tore his Achilles in Week 7 of the 2024 season. Watson went 5 of 12 for 36 yards and an interception during Cleveland's eventual 31-7 loss. "I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance," Watson said. "It's a little bit more personal than that. So, I think it's a disrespectful thing."To make his point, Watson noted that Saturday wasn't the first time that he felt the ire of Browns fans. He added that he gets treated better by opposing fans. 
 "Last time I played on this field, I tore my Achilles. That same fan base, they cheered when I got hurt," he said. "What does that have to do with anything about performance? When a person gets hurt, especially in your home stadium, and they cheer."Watson said that his experiences with Browns fans are usually only negative on either social media or during home games. He was hoping that the situation regarding the fans' treatment of him would be better given his involvement in the city and after he worked to get himself back in position to compete to be the Browns' starting quarterback. "I thought being away for two years and working myself back from two Achilles injuries and putting the time in and being around the facility, being around the city, doing charity work in the city, supporting the Cleveland Browns, hanging out with fans whenever I do see them, being honest, being the type of person that I know I am and the character would help," he said. "And I guess it hasn't. So that's why I say it's personal. So it is what it is. People have their own opinions. There's only so much you can do to change that. So at the end of the day, I just have to continue to just work on it and strive to be better mentally moving forward."  
Saturday was a continuation of the downward spiral that has been Watson's career, especially since he arrived in Cleveland in 2022. A three-time Pro Bowler with the Texans, injuries and inconsistent play have plagued Watson throughout his time with the Browns. He is 9-10 as the Browns' starting quarterback with just 19 touchdowns, 12 interceptions and a mediocre 61.2% completion percentage. Adding to the frustration that has been Watson's story in Cleveland is the amount of capital the Browns spent to get him. They sent Houston six draft picks that included three consecutive first-round picks in addition to signing Watson to a record-setting, five-year, $230 million fully guaranteed contract. It's undeniably one of -- if not the -- worst transactions in the history of sports.  There's also the fact that the Browns traded for Watson despite the fact that he had already been sued by over two dozen female massage therapists for sexual harassment and sexual assault (in 2022, it was announced that 20 of the 24 women who sued Watson had reached confidential settlements). Watson's time in Cleveland began with him serving an 11-game suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy. 
In addition to Watson's plight, the fact that he's competing against the immensely popular Sanders doesn't help his cause. Sanders, who made the Pro Bowl as a rookie, went 9 of 11 for 74 yards with a touchdown and an interception against the Bills. Sanders also shone during his postgame press conference when he was asked about the fans' treatment of Watson. "I think we all need to understand that we're all human," he said. "I don't really do things to humans I wouldn't want done to me. ... Just for our fans, I appreciate y'all showing up and everything. However y'all feel about the situation, about Deshaun, I think it's more about a bigger purpose than just respect. The respect thing that I feel like should be there. Because we're out trying to do our best and trying to serve the franchise the best way possible. We're going out there every game and doing everything we can do. I don't really appreciate that." As noted above, Watson didn't do himself any favors both during and after Saturday's game. And while Monken said that his postgame comments won't impact his decision, Watson's response when asked if he can play through more boos from Browns fans if he wins the starting job should be cause for concern. 
"I don't know," he said. "It's a mental battle every day. I feel like I get more love on road games than I do home games. If it is my spot and he does makes me the [starter], maybe it's 17 away games then. I don't know."

title: Randy Arozarena becomes third in MLB history with first-pitch home run, walk-off homer -- just days after PCA - CBS Sports
description: Arozarena also robbed a home run in the Mariners' win over the Cubs on Saturday
body:
Arozarena also robbed a home run in the Mariners' win over the Cubs on Saturday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Mere days after Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs became the second player to hit a first-pitch home run and a walk-off home run in the same game, Randy Arozarena of the Mariners became the third – coincidentally, at the expense of PCA's Cubs. 
Arozarena on Saturday hit the opening pitch of the bottom of the first – a sinker from David Peterson – 416 feet to center for a 1-0 Seattle lead and his 18th home run of the season. Much later, in the bottom of the ninth, Arozarena came up with two on, two out and the Mariners down by a pair of runs. Arozarena delivered in the hugest way with a game-winning blast off a Jacob Webb slider that, even more coincidentally, soared over the glove of PCA out in center and gave the hosts a crucial 5-4 win. This is to say nothing of Arozerena's home run robbery earlier in the game, which means his entire evening on the job merits a look: In all, Arozarena was 3 for 4 with a walk and those pair of homers, and all of it was essential to Seattle's thrilling win. The 31-year-old three-time All-Star is now slashing .275/.369/.463 on the season, which is good for an OPS+ of 139. Arozarena also leads the Mariners in WAR with a figure of 4.3.
"I think it's my biggest game," Arozarena said after the game through an interpreter (via MLB.com). "I didn't expect to come into the game and hit two home runs and rob one. But yes, it was a special day for me, a special performance for myself. But most importantly, this moment in time for the team and being able to help the team win is the biggest thing for today."For his bit of history, Arozarena is now just the seventh player since 1900 to hit a leadoff home run and a walk-off home run in the same game: PlayerDateOpponentRandy Arozarena, MarinersAug. 22, 2026 				CubsPete Crow-Armstrong, Cubs 				Aug. 17, 2026 				White Sox 				Chris Young, Diamondbacks 				Aug. 7, 2010 				Padres 				Ian Kinsler, Rangers 				July 19, 2009 				Twins 				Reed Johnson, Blue Jays 				June 15, 2003 				Cubs 				Darin Erstad, Angels 				June 25, 2000 				Twins 				Vic Power, KC Athletics 				May 7, 1957 				Orioles 				That he hit that leadoff home run on the first pitch puts him in even more exclusive company. As noted above, just PCA and Vic Power in 1957 had achieved that feat before Arozarena joined them on Saturday night in Seattle. 
Arozarena's heroics improved the Mariners to 62-68 on the season. While that's a disappointing record for the club that made it to the ALCS last year, they're also just three games behind the Astros in the AL West. They also remain in the chase for the third and final wild-card spot in the AL.

        The penultimate event on the 2026 PGA Tour schedule brought the top 50 in the FedEx Cup standings to Bellerive Country Club in St. Louis for the BMW Championship. As was the case at last week's St. Jude Championship, another $20 million purse was on the line.With just 50 players in the field this week, everyone was guaranteed at least $66,000 with the top 40 all earning at least a six-figure payday. The winner, Wyndham Clark, will take home a $3.6 million paycheck, as the playoff events boast the same purse structure as the non-cut signature events on the PGA Tour schedule. Clark won for the thir time this season and sixth time in his PGA Tour career, putting himself in legitimate contention for Player of the Year honors -- especially if he can close the season strong at next week's Tour Championship.Players were not only jockeying for payouts from the BMW Championship purse this week. They were angling for spots in the FedEx Cup standings, which will determine their share of the massive bonus pool that is paid out before next week's Tour Championship. That alone boasts a $40 million purse and pays $10 million to the winnerLast week's winner, Scottie Scheffler, locked himself into the top spot in the standings, guaranteeing a $23 million bonus no matter where he finishes Sunday at the BMW Championship. Clark moved into the No. 3 spot after the BMW Championship.

body:
The former NBA player has requested eligibility for the WNBA draft amid the row over transgender inclusion in the league
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:59 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        CHICAGO -- Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from his courtside seat during the Indiana Fever's 113-90 win over the Chicago Sky on Sunday after getting into a verbal altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud. Late in the third quarter, Cloud drove to the basket and converted a tough finish that drew a timeout from Fever coach Stephanie White. As players from both teams went to their respective benches, Cloud began pointing and yelling at Kanter Freedom, who stood up and walked toward the court. An official and security personnel immediately jumped in, and Cloud's teammates arrived to pull her away from the situation. The official gestured for Kanter Freedom to be ejected and both team and arena security escorted him away from his seat. He tried to protest in an area behind the courtside seating for a short period before eventually leaving to a chorus of boos and middle fingers.Natasha Cloud did not speak with the media after Sunday's game. She did meet with team and league security.
"I talked to the team and Tash didn't want to feel like she was a distraction. I told her she wasn't," Sky coach Tyler Marsh said in his post-game press conference. "I told her we all embrace her as someone who protects our team and people who need to be protected. Tash is always gonna stand on that and we stand for Tash.""There's so many good things about this league and so many good things about the play of these players, that if you come to a game, you should probably come to enjoy the basketball," Marsh said. "That seems pretty simple to me. I think these players deserve that and have earned that. Being a former basketball player, you should probably understand and feel that too."
Fever star Caitlin Clark said that she did not see the incident, and both she and Lexie Hull shook their heads no when asked if Kanter Freedom had said anything to them during the game. Fever coach Stephanie White said that it is "important that people like you guys in this room don't give it any gas. It's a social media thing."
This is not the first time that Cloud and Kanter Freedom have crossed paths. In 2023, the two went back and forth on social media after Cloud criticized the United States government.  The WNBA has become a battleground for the debate about transgender athletes over the last month after Fever guard Sophie Cunningham said in an ESPN profile that she wants to "protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men." Later, Cunningham doubled down prior to the Fever's win over the Connecticut Sun on July 22. "I said what I said. I think it's kind of common sense," she said. "And I think I'll always believe in that. I think it's really important to protect children, and that's little girls who are also involved in that category. I stand on what I said."
Cunningham added that she doesn't "dislike anyone" and that there's "room to love everyone." She continued, "I'm also there to love biological women, and I think that there are rights that need to be protected. And, like I said, I'm gonna stand true to that. I'll never falter in my beliefs in that. But I have never once stated that I hated the trans community."In the wake of Cunningham's comments, Kanter Freedom has spent the past few weeks agitating to be eligible for the 2027 WNBA Draft, along with fellow former NBA player Royce White. Both Kanter Freedom and White have claimed that they now identify as women. The WNBA has never had a transgender player and does not have a public policy about transgender participation. The new collective bargaining agreement states simply that, "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA." 
Earlier this month, the WNBA convened a task force to discuss the issue and made a statement that read, in part, "We will approach these important conversations thoughtfully and in alignment with the values of our league. There are no immediate eligibility matters affecting the WNBA, and we strongly denounce the bad-faith efforts to use these topics to demean or marginalize others."

title: NFL preseason Week 2 overreactions: Shedeur Sanders will start for Browns, Jets' defense is fixed - CBS Sports
description: Not everything that unfolded in the second batch of preseason action is worth reading into
body:
Not everything that unfolded in the second batch of preseason action is worth reading into
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:15 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL preseason is ripe for overreactions. Much of what unfolds on game days should be taken with a grain of salt as teams hold back the "good stuff" from their playbooks and rest their starters. At the same time, some of the offseason's most important decisions come down to these games. Such is the case in Cleveland, where the Browns might have settled their quarterback competition after a preseason Week 2 eyesore from Deshaun Watson and a solid showing from Shedeur Sanders.Sanders may be the biggest winner from the second set of preseason games. De'Zhaun Stribling could be on his way to a stellar rookie season with the 49ers if Thursday's display of receiving prowess was any indication. And the Jets' defense actually looks… competitive?Not all of those takeaways are guaranteed to play out come the regular season. Some of what unfolded in the second week of the preseason will go down as mere exhibition fallout rather than meaningful data.Let's separate overreactions from reality.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Shedeur Sanders will be the Browns' starting quarterbackThe plan was always for Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders to get one start apiece to open the preseason. Now that Todd Monken has the data points he set out to acquire, a decision on which of the two will open the regular season atop the depth chart is imminent. In fact, it could come as soon as Monday. And after Watson's disastrous showing on Saturday, it is hard to picture the veteran winning the job.
It is not as if Sanders went out and won the job himself. He threw an interception in each of his first two preseason outings and was underwhelming in Week 1, albeit with a decent bounce-back effort (9-for-11, 74 yards, one touchdown, one interception) in Week 2. The potential pecking order in Cleveland is more a product of Watson looking unplayable on Saturday.While Watson outplayed Sanders a week ago, he floundered in his most recent appearance with poorly placed throws and a 5-for-12, 35-yard stat line with an interception. Browns fans booed him off the field, and while Monken said Watson's postgame comments toward the Cleveland faithful will not impact the starting quarterback decision, they were a poor look.Verdict: Reality
                            
    
                                                
                    
    De'Zhaun Stribling will win Offensive Rookie of the YearIt has been difficult to find uplifting storylines from 49ers camp due to their onslaught of injuries, but De'Zhaun Stribling's emergence as a potentially game-changing rookie is as pleasant a development as any in the Bay Area. A week after he racked up seven catches for 63 yards as the leader of San Francisco's receiving unit, Stribling tied with KhaDarel Hodge for the most catches (four) and yards (46) of any 49er on Thursday.
Importantly, three of those catches came on connections with starting quarterback Brock Purdy. The two were on the same page from the get-go in the rout of the Chargers and strung together three completions on the opening drive. Stribling then hauled in a 21-yard grab from Mac Jones on the team's second possession.Stribling, the No. 33 overall pick in April's draft, saw his Rookie of the Year odds spike. Per DraftKings, his +1100 odds are the fifth-shortest behind only Jeremiyah Love, Jadarian Price, Fernando Mendoza and Carnell Tate. He has been as productive as any of them this preseason, but the sheer volume of contenders for the award (and the fact that Love and Price, at least, figure to hold larger roles) still means he will have to outperform expectations to win the honor.Verdict: Overreaction… but possible!
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tua Tagovailoa should watch his backTua Tagovailoa threw just three passes in the first week of the preseason and watched Saturday's 34-6 drubbing of the Colts from the sideline. That is a starter's preseason workload. His grasp on the role is tenuous, though.
Neither Cooper Rush nor Jack Strand will unseat Tagovailoa from the starting job, but the Falcons have to appreciate what they combined to deliver in this week's offensive showcase. Strand, an undrafted rookie, racked up 212 passing yards, 22 rushing yards and a touchdown both through the air and on the ground. Cooper Rush went 10-for-11.The real threat to Tagovailoa is twofold. First, he has been underwhelming in camp. Second, Michael Penix Jr. is cleared for 11-on-11 work and figures to make a run at the job. This always figured to be a two-man battle, and now that Penix is healthy, he has about three weeks to make up ground and potentially leap past his fellow southpaw. His momentum from 7-on-7 and individual drills gives him a shot to do so.Verdict: Reality
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jets' defense is fixedThe Jets' defense infamously went the entire 2025 season without recording an interception. The group secured two takeaways in one game during Week 2 of the preseason. Andre Cisco, who is in the mix for a starting role at one of the safety spots, hauled in the first one while reserve cornerback Samuel Womack III grabbed the second. Both came against Steelers quarterback Will Howard.
Toss in a David Bailey sack, two sacks from Nate Lynn and another from Chase Wilson, and it was a banner day for New York. The starting unit played into the second quarter of a game in which the Steelers went scoreless.Remember, though, that this came against Pittsburgh's No. 2 offense. And keep in mind that while the Jets overhauled the unit with a plethora of free agent additions, none of them are elite players. Aaron Glenn needs this group to hold its own in 2026, and it may just do that. But this shutout means very little.Verdict: Overreaction
                            
    
                                                
                    
    J.J. McCarthy is not Minnesota's second-best quarterbackWhen J.J. McCarthy fell short of Kyler Murray in the competition for the Vikings' starting quarterback duties, the reasonable conclusion was that he would settle in as the No. 2 option in the group. Even that might be a stretch for the third-year pro at this point. He had a rough go of it against the Ravens' defense on Saturday; across 18 snaps, he completed just five of 10 passes, took three hits and fell victim to a sack.
Coach Kevin O'Connell said that McCarthy would have played longer if not for being "banged up" during his limited work. That highlights another issue with the former first-round pick: he simply cannot stay healthy.While O'Connell said a week ago that McCarthy is Minnesota's No. 2 quarterback, it is increasingly clear that he does not have a long-term future in this offense. Carson Wentz might give the Vikings a better chance of winning games if Murray misses any time.Verdict: Reality
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Packers solved their kicking woesThe search to find a successor to Mason Crosby since his departure in 2022 has been anything but smooth for the Packers. It appears that they finally have an answer, however. They were the only team to use a draft pick on a kicker in 2026, and it looks like an astute move. Sixth-rounder Trey Smack has been a preseason standout.
In Week 1, Smack drilled a 58-yard field goal and matched that distance on a kick that was ultimately waved off for a defensive penalty. He went 3-for-3 in his professional debut. That was just the start of it. He was even better this week and made all four of his field goal attempts, with two coming from more than 50 yards out. His longest was a 59-yard blast.After a year in which Green Bay missed four extra points and was as reliable as a coin flip on kicks beyond 50 yards, special teams could suddenly be a legitimate weapon.Verdict: Reality
